awards.title: Best Model
awards.description: Models and computer simulations can help us understand the function and operation of BioBrick Parts and Devices. Simulation and modeling are critical engineering skills that can contribute to project design or provide a better understanding of the modeled process. These processes are even more useful and/or informative when real world data are included in the model. This award is for teams who build a model of their system and use it to inform system design or simulate expected behavior before, or in conjunction with, experiments in the wetlab.

awards.title: Best Presentation
awards.description: Presentations should be clear, engaging, and communicate your project to a scientific/engineering community. Can your team tell your story and present your data in a concise and visually appealing way?

awards.title: Best Software Tool
awards.description: iGEM projects often rely on the creation or adaptation of computational tools that drive progress. These tools, born from practical needs, can sometimes offer unexpected value to others. Whether simple or complex, they can play a crucial role in a project's success. This award recognizes impactful software tools or computational methods that make a significant contribution. To be eligible, your software must be well-documented and made available under an OSI-approved open-source license.

awards.title: Best Agriculture Project
awards.description: In the coming decades, agriculture must both feed the growing global population and implement sustainable practices to ensure a healthy environment. This challenge has become more difficult as the increased frequency and intensity of extreme weather events has led to lower crop yields, reduced soil fertility, and more pests and diseases. How will your team apply synthetic biology to revolutionize agriculture and improve the quality and quantity of food?

awards.title: Best Space Project
awards.description: Carl Sagan once said mankind will be forced to leave planet Earth to survive in the long run, but there are gargantuan technical challenges associated with space exploration that need to be solved. How can synthetic biology tackle the challenges astronauts will face in the coming years, from in situ resource utilization and space cybernetics to terraforming Mars?

awards.title: Best Sustainable Development Impact
awards.description: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are a call to action to integrally address global environmental, social, and economic challenges. iGEM teams can answer this call with this prize. Demonstrate how you have evaluated your project ideas against one or more of the SDGs, how you've consulted with SDG stakeholders, and how you've begun to form collaborations with other iGEM teams around the SDGs. You're encouraged to look back at previous iGEM projects to evaluate them against the SDGs and build upon them.

awards.title: Best Wiki
awards.description: The team Wiki is the “face” of your iGEM project. The team Wikis serve as the main project information resource for future iGEM students and teams, as well as the rest of the world. This award honors the team Wiki that exemplifies what the following year's Wikis should strive for.

awards.title: Best New Basic Part
awards.description: Most genetically-encoded functions have not yet been converted to BioBrick parts. Thus, there are many opportunities to find new, cool, and important genetically encoded functions, and refine and convert the DNA encoding these functions into BioBrick standard biological parts. To be eligible for this award, this part will consist of a single genetic component and be supported by documentation on the Main Page on the Part's Page on the Registry. Winning parts are highly documented with experimental details and data showing the part working. See parts BBa_K863006 and BBa_K863001 as examples.

awards.title: Safety and Security Award
awards.description: Synthetic biology will need to be used safely and securely if local people are to solve local problems all around the world. The Safety and Security Committee is challenging teams to apply biological engineering approaches to manage risks associated with synthetic biology. Can you take the next step in incremental progress towards knowledge, understanding, and tools that will make the use of synthetic biology safer and more secure?

awards.title: Best Oncology Project
awards.description:
With 1 in 5 people diagnosed with cancer during their lifetime, nearly every family globally is affected by this disease.
Can synthetic biology help end cancer as we know it by creating solutions for early detection and treatment, boosting the survival rate, and ensuring access to quality services for cancer prevention and care?

awards.title: Best New Composite Part
awards.description: New BioBrick devices can be made by combining existing BioBrick Parts. For example, Inverters, Amplifiers, Smell Generators, Protein Balloon Generators, Senders, Receivers, Actuators, and so on. To be eligible for this award, this part will consist of a combination of genetic components and be supported by documentation on the Main Page on the Part's Page on the Registry. Winning parts are highly documented with experimental details and data showing the part working. See parts BBa_K404122 and BBa_K863005 as examples.

awards.title: Best Integrated Human Practices
awards.description: How does your project affect society and how does society influence the direction of your project? How might ethical considerations and stakeholder input guide your project purpose, design, and experiments you conduct in the lab? How does this feedback enter into the process of your work all through the iGEM competition? Document a thoughtful and creative approach to exploring these questions and how your project evolved in the process to compete for this award.

awards.title: Best Education
awards.description: How have you developed new opportunities to include more people in shaping synthetic biology? Innovative educational tools and outreach activities have the ability to establish a two-way dialogue with new communities by discussing public values and the science behind synthetic biology. Document your approach and what was learned by everyone involved to compete for this award.

awards.description: Many medical conditions can be successfully treated if only they are diagnosed at an early enough stage. Diagnostic technologies also play a key role in preventive healthcare, public health, and epidemiology. Can your team come up with faster, cheaper and better diagnostics techniques to improve access to medical treatment worldwide?

Whether your team built a sensor to help characterize parts or designed a robot to streamline experiments and cloning, this prize recognizes innovative hardware that supports the synthetic biology community.
